quizzes.title: Early Life & Education — Knowledge Checkpoint
quizzes.intro: Answer to unlock your checkpoint stamp. Explanations follow every answer.

questions.question: Where was Dr. B. R. Ambedkar born on 14 April 1891?
questions.explanation: He was born at Mhow in the Central Provinces, a army cantonment town where his father served. The site is today the Dr. Ambedkar Janmabhoomi memorial.

questions.question: Which scholarship took Ambedkar to Columbia University in 1913?
answers: A Baroda State scholarship from Sayajirao Gaekwad III
questions.explanation: The Maharaja of Baroda, Sayajirao Gaekwad III, funded his studies at Columbia University, where he earned his M.A. (1915) and later his Ph.D.

questions.question: Ambedkar held doctorates in economics from both Columbia University and the University of London (LSE).
questions.explanation: He earned a Ph.D. from Columbia University and a D.Sc. (Economics) from the University of London in 1923 — one of the most qualified scholars of his generation.

questions.question: Arrange these milestones in chronological order:
questions.explanation: Matriculation 1907 → B.A. 1912 → Columbia 1913 → D.Sc. 1923. Education was the through-line of his entire life.

quizzes.title: Social Reform — Match & Verify
quizzes.intro: Check your grasp of the reform movement.

questions.question: Match each event to its year:
questions.explanation: The movement ran in parallel streams: journalism (1920), direct non-violent action (1927–30), electoral negotiation (1932) and party politics (1936).

questions.question: What did the Poona Pact (1932) establish for the depressed classes?
questions.explanation: The Pact, reached while Gandhi fasted in Yerwada Jail, replaced separate electorates with reserved seats in joint electorates — the ancestor of today's legislative reservations.

questions.question: The March 1927 satyagraha at Mahad asserted the right to…
answers: Draw water from the public Chavdar Tank
questions.explanation: The non-violent satyagraha at Mahad's Chavdar Tank asserted the basic civic right of so-called untouchables to use public water.

quizzes.title: Law & Constitution — The Preamble Challenge
quizzes.intro: Read the Preamble at the Constitution Table, then test yourself.

questions.question: Which principle does the phrase 'EQUALITY of status and of opportunity' most directly represent in the Preamble?
questions.explanation: The Preamble secures four ideals: JUSTICE (social, economic, political), LIBERTY (of thought, expression, belief, faith, worship), EQUALITY (of status and opportunity), and FRATERNITY (assuring dignity of the individual and unity of the nation).

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes untouchability?
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes 'untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form. Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21 protect equality before law, non-discrimination, freedoms, and life & personal liberty respectively.

questions.question: Ambedkar called Article 32 — constitutional remedies — 'the very soul of the Constitution'. What does Article 32 guarantee?
answers: The right to move the Supreme Court to enforce fundamental rights
questions.explanation: Article 32 lets any citizen directly approach the Supreme Court to enforce fundamental rights — which is why he called it the heart and soul of the Constitution (Constituent Assembly Debates, Vol. VII).

questions.question: Order these constitutional events:
questions.explanation: Fifteen days after Independence, Ambedkar was chosen to chair the Drafting Committee; adoption came on 26 Nov 1949 and enforcement on 26 Jan 1950.

questions.question: The Preamble begins with the words 'WE, THE PEOPLE OF INDIA'.
questions.explanation: The Preamble opens 'WE, THE PEOPLE OF INDIA…', proclaiming that constitutional authority flows from the people themselves.

quizzes.title: FINAL KNOWLEDGE CHALLENGE — Heritage Archivist Examination
quizzes.intro: The final challenge draws on every gallery. Earn the title: HERITAGE ARCHIVIST.

questions.question: Identify the memorial: the site of the 14 October 1956 mass conversion to Buddhism in Nagpur is today called…
questions.explanation: Deekshabhoomi, Nagpur, marks the 1956 conversion ground; its great hollow stupa was designed by architect Sheo Dan Mal. Chaitya Bhoomi (Mumbai) is the cremation-site memorial.

questions.question: Which work began as an invited address that was never delivered because the organizers withdrew the invitation?
questions.explanation: The Jat-Pat Todak Mandal cancelled Ambedkar's presidential address after reading its uncompromising text; he published it himself as 'Annihilation of Caste'.

questions.question: Ambedkar's doctoral dissertation at LSE, published 1923, analyzed which subject?
answers: Indian currency and exchange — 'The Problem of the Rupee'
questions.explanation: 'The Problem of the Rupee: Its Origin and Its Solution' studied India's currency system and is cited among the works anticipating the case for a central bank.

questions.question: Final timeline — order the whole arc:
questions.explanation: 1891 → 1927 → 1932 → 1949 → 1956: from birth in a cantonment town to the Constitution, and finally to a new spiritual path. You now hold the full arc.

questions.question: Dr. Ambedkar was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1990.
questions.explanation: He received India's highest civilian honour in 1990, thirty-four years after his Mahaparinirvan on 6 December 1956.

questions.question: Match the memorial to its city:
questions.explanation: Birth (Mhow), reform ground (many cities), cremation memorial (Mumbai), conversion ground (Nagpur), final residence (Delhi) — together they map a life.
